newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO resume joint patrols in Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO resume joint patrols in Bethlehem.

text.p: Israel and the PLO resumed joint military patrols in the West Bank town of Bethlehem on Thursday ahead of Christmas and two months after the patrols were suspended following bloody clashes, the Israeli army said.
"This morning the joint patrols of the Israeli army and the Palestinian police in the city of Bethlehem were renewed and are operating as they did before September 1996," the statement said.
Under an interim peace deal, Israeli and Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) forces patrol main roads through the six West Bank cities which Israel handed to the PLO last year.

Joint patrols were suspended after Palestinian police and Israeli troops plunged into gun battles in September during demonstrations over Israeli policies in Jerusalem. Sixty Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed in the clashes.
The Israeli army statement said the town of Bethlehem, traditional birthplace of Jesus, remains closed to Israelis until further notice.
